That is not missing content, it is a missing join, and it is the objection this package makes to others - you declared coverage without joining each requirement to the place that answers it - turned on the scorecard itself. compliance_matrix.json now carries a rubric_coverage section joining each of the seven dimensions to the sections that answer it, 21 section references in all, and saying in both languages that it is a map and not a claim about the score. Two things about how it is built. The dimension list is read from upstream/main on every build rather than copied, so if the organisers add or rename a dimension the map fails to cover it and the build stops - the lesson E132 had just taught. And every one of the 21 section references must resolve against a heading in proposal.md, because a map whose destinations have been renamed is worse than no map: it still looks like navigation while sending the reader somewhere that is not there, and this package has already shipped four dead machine-readable anchors of that shape. After this fix, 7 dimensions and 21 references all resolve, and M34 - changing one word of one section name - takes the harness to 34 mutations.
summaries.E134: The review tool loads data/source_registry.json and hands the model a summary of it, telling it to use that to separate sources usable for formal conclusions from background-only and provisional ones. The registry holds nine sources. This package cites eight of them - all by URL, under its own ids, with no field joining the two. A package whose whole argument is that a claim must be joined to its evidence by machine had left the organisers' own registry to be matched by eye. And the two classifications disagreed once, in this package's favour: the State Council implementing plan on smart-technology difficulties for older people is usable_for_formal background_only in the registry, and this package graded it regulatory_baseline, its strongest class, and rested a non-waivable constraint on it. Where a published contract and a self-assessment disagree the contract governs, all the more when the divergence flatters the package. The constraint does not depend on it: the first row of the same table already rests on article 39 of the Barrier-Free Environment Construction Law, which the registry grades approved and formal-usable, and the policy document carries a narrower sentence. Three changes. Every one of the nine records matching the registry now carries organizer_registry_id, so the two lists the reviewer receives can be aligned mechanically. The policy document drops from regulatory_baseline to background_only, matching the registry's cap, with a bilingual note on why it moved and that it is still cited but no longer carries a formal conclusion. And a new gate, registry_alignment_qa, checks both directions - a source matching the registry must record the registry id, and this package's grade may not exceed the strength the registry allows - reading the registry from upstream/main, the lesson E120 and E132 each taught once, and saying which side it read. After this fix, 9 sources aligned and none overstated, and M35 - restoring the stronger grade - takes the harness to 35 mutations across 19 of 19 gates.
summaries.E135: The English edition went over the 256 KiB intake cap and this package's own build printed BUILD OK. What caught it was the organisers' validate_submission.py - Markdown files must be <= 262144 bytes - which is the one check a submission cannot afford to be corrected by. Two things were behind it. First, the build's size check only ever printed: it reports the headroom, marks the line tight below 4 KiB, and does nothing at all when the headroom goes negative. The comment beside that code says the cap was once hit as a build failure because nothing said how close it was - so the reporting was added and the failure was not kept. Second, what pushed it over: the errata register's shape table bolded any shape whose count reached five, and each crossing costs eight bytes in each edition. The register growing made the proposal grow, which is nobody's chosen relationship and is the same shape as E98, a correctness that rests on a numeric coincidence and tightens as the package grows. A limit that is announced and never enforced is a limit that cannot be failed, a shape this register has recorded seven times and which this time landed on itself. The bolding is gone from both editions - the count column already says which shapes are common, and the asterisks said it twice while charging for the repetition - recovering 88 bytes per edition and leaving the English with 82 after this fix. The size check now fails the build when a file is over, and is named in the expression that decides the overall verdict, which is the rule already written beside it. One self-sustaining state was cleared along the way: self_check.json had been written once with DETERMINISTIC_VALIDATION failed, and since that file is itself validated, the failure kept revalidating itself. The build already neutralises the entry before measuring, and that step works - the real cause was the oversize English edition, not the loop. The organisers' validator now returns Result: PASS.
summaries.E136: E135 turned the Markdown cap from a line that reported headroom into one that fails the build. But it sits in build_all's main, and the mutation harness runs gates, not the build - so the failure path just added had nothing proving it would ever fire. This package requires every gate to be shown capable of failing, for the reason that a gate which has never failed and a gate which cannot fail look exactly alike, and the newest fix was in precisely that state. What it guards is also the least forgiving thing in the package: the intake caps are enforced by the organisers' validator, where being corrected means the submission is refused. The check moved into a gate of its own, intake_limits_qa, which walks every shipped Markdown and JSON file against the organisers' two caps and reports how much room the tightest one has left - after this fix, 44 files within the caps and proposal.en.md tightest with 82 bytes to spare. build_all keeps its headroom reporting, which is for a human, and the verdict comes from the gate. M36 appends 200 bytes to the English edition to push it over, and the gate names it, taking the harness to 36 mutations across 20 of 20 gates. The same question was asked of the whole build: every quantity computed in main and left out of the expression that decides the verdict was checked one by one, and only one looked missing - the organisers' self-check, whose result reaches the expression through a differently named variable. Everything else was already counted. A fix that cannot be shown to fire is the same announcement moved to a new file.
summaries.E137: A reviewer sees only the first page of each PDF, which makes A0 board 1 and the A3 cover the two scarcest surfaces in the package - chosen by this build, replaced by nothing else. When board 1 was reordered the reasoning went into a comment: a slot spent on a sheet that already travels as its own PNG buys nothing. And in that same comment block one sentence still said boards 1-3 were the rasterised ones, the reading corrected twelve lines above it. One comment held both versions of one fact, and the surviving stale half was precisely the one that would have justified spending the scarce slot on a repeat. The reasoning lived only in prose and nothing enforced it. Following that turned up two counting faults. The coverage line says N gates are not yet proven able to fail, each with its reason published, and N was the length of UNCOVERED while the genuinely unproven set is all_gates minus the proven ones. Those two coincided until a gate was added that no mutation of a shipped file can reach, so for one build the sentence promised a published reason for a gate that had none. Below that: evidence_ceiling.py is a real gate - it refuses any metric graded above its weakest input and M26 proves it - and it sat outside the denominator because its name does not end in _qa.py. E121 made the denominator read the build, and it read only the part of the build matching a naming convention, printing 20 of 21 while 22 ran. The stale sentence is gone and the rule is now the gate scarce_surface_qa: no sheet on the rasterised board may be one of the five figures the harness already sends, that list read from upstream/main. After this fix board 1 carries identity and kit-of-parts, neither among the five. The six boards' composition collapses into one BOARD_SHEETS list, five of them having been literals beside a constant naming all six. Both counting faults are repaired: the unproven set is computed, every unproven gate must carry a reason in UNCOVERED or the build fails, the denominator gains a register for gates not named _qa with their reasons, and an assertion now requires anything the harness proves to be inside the denominator it is proved against - which catches this exact mistake. After this fix: 20 of 22 gates proven, 2 unproven each with its reason, and 20 plus 2 is 22.
summaries.E138: Following E137's question - what else has a denominator decided by a naming convention? The deliverable-naming gate globs three data extensions and covers the four finished documents through a short hand-written list. What that list got wrong was not omission but the opposite: it required both editions to name the same Chinese document. So the English edition pointed at the Chinese A3 booklet, the Chinese A0 boards, the Chinese HTML page and the Chinese visual index, while a3-booklet.en.pdf, a0-boards.en.pdf, proposal.en.html and index.en.html shipped and were named by neither edition. An English reader was sent to an A3 booklet in Chinese while the booklet meant for them sat in the package unmentioned. Naming a document is only useful to a reader of the language it is written in, and the old rule looked stricter - name it in both - while being the reason the English edition pointed the wrong way. A stricter rule is not the same as a correct one. These four are also what a reviewer actually opens, since the PDF first pages and the HTML screenshots are among what the harness sends, which makes this the shape recorded twelve times here: a deliverable that was never looked at as a deliverable before shipping. The English edition now points at the English documents, 12 bytes against headroom computed first and 69 left after. The four move out of the shared list into a language-paired rule checked per edition - the Chinese edition names the Chinese file, the English names the .en file, and a missing one fails the build. The flat list is 54 after this fix, with 8 finished documents, four in each of two languages, checked per edition. M37 points the English edition back at the Chinese booklet and the gate names it, taking the harness to 37 mutations.
summaries.E139: Asking the branch-is-a-stale-snapshot question of the taskbook itself: brief/site-package/agent_taskbook.json differs from upstream/main by 16 lines, and the whole missing section is called multimodal_presentation. summaries.E141: E139 and E140 came from one cause, so it was worth asking exhaustively: how far behind upstream are the organisers' files in this repository? That registry is revised on the organisers' schedule while this branch reads a snapshot from before #2149 - the same cause that had already cost this package an entire section of delivery requirements in E139 and a whole second set of review dimensions in E140. If a mandatory standard were added, the matrix would silently fail to answer it, and preventing exactly that is what the words compliance matrix mean. The new gate, standards_alignment_qa, checks both directions: every standard the organisers mark mandatory must appear in standard_matrix.json, and every standard id this package cites must exist in the registry, since citing an id the reader cannot resolve is the claimed-a-source-it-could-not-name shape recorded twice here. summaries.E142: E141 recorded that upstream ships the full texts of three statutes this branch does not have, and said checking this package's quotations against them was next. Checked: one of the three is wrong, and wrong in the part that matters. Article 39 of the Barrier-Free Environment Construction Law reads that public service venues handling medical care, social security, financial business or utility payment matters shall retain traditional service methods including on-site guidance and manual handling. This package rendered it as venues providing medical, insurance, financial and water/electricity/gas services - social security written as insurance, utility payments as water, electricity and gas, two categories replaced by narrower ones the statute does not use, and the same error in both editions. The clause the argument turns on was verbatim; the list of what that clause covers was not. The other two check out: article 14 of the generative-AI interim measures matches word for word, article 15 is a faithful abridgement whose load-bearing phrase about publishing the handling process and response time limit is verbatim, and the elderly smart-technology plan's line about keeping traditional service methods alongside intelligent innovation is exact. What makes the one error serious is its job: it is carried as the legal basis for a constraint this proposal calls non-waivable. Narrowing social security to insurance invites a reader to think the article governs commercial insurance settings; narrowing utility payments to water, electricity and gas drops other payment matters the article covers. A quotation is the one kind of claim that cannot be argued about - the text either says it or it does not - and this package's whole position is that a claim no machine can check is not evidence. Nothing had ever checked it, because the text needed to check it was not in this branch. Both editions now carry the statute's own words, at 39 bytes in Chinese and 20 in English against headroom computed first, leaving 48. The new gate, statute_quote_qa, requires every statutory sentence this package quotes to appear verbatim in the text the organisers ship, normalising only whitespace and the enumeration comma, and to still appear in the proposal, since a check guarding a sentence that has been deleted is guarding nothing. The texts are read from upstream/main and the readout says which side. After this fix: 3 statutes, 4 quotations, all verbatim. The comparison is a multiset rather than a set: five requirement texts are asked by two tasks, so a set collapses 63 to 58, and the first version did exactly that and printed all 58 requirements inside a sentence that says 63 - the presence-instead-of-multiset mistake this register has recorded once already. summaries.E144: Continuing through the upstream files E141 named and had not read. brief/source-quality-rules.md carries an English quick reference upstream that this checkout lacks - and the Chinese tables it summarises have been here all along: authority levels A0 primary, A1 strong, A2 supporting, A3 benchmark and X never index, timeliness levels T0 to T4, a crawl priority order, and a rule that figures, scope and periods should be cited from A0. This package's 22 sources had never been described in that published grading; they were only ever graded on the five-step evidence ceiling this package invented. This one is not a case of being unable to read the rule - the file is in this checkout with its Chinese tables complete - but of never applying it, while this package insists elsewhere on speaking the organisers' published vocabulary, in E134 for the source registry and E141 for the standards registry. X matters most: commercial map tiles, account-gated or password-protected material, unclear-copyright images, non-public drawings and personal information. A source in X does not belong in a submission at all, not merely in this list. All 22 now carry an authority level and a timeliness level: 20 sit in A0 to A3, with the organisers' own documents and the statutes at A0 and the six international cases at A3, and 2 say they are outside what the table describes, with reasons - OpenStreetMap is crowd-sourced geography, neither official publication nor authorised republication nor a benchmark institution's report, and this package's own census is its own measurement rather than public material. Refusing to force a level that does not fit is closer to the rule's purpose than forcing one. Each was checked against X and none falls there. sources_qa now requires every source to carry a level or explain why the table does not describe it, fails the build on any source graded X, and requires a timeliness level alongside every A0-A3 grade, because an authority level alone says nothing about whether the document still stands.
